### HTML and CSS in Markdown

- If you need "inline <span style="color:red">colored</span> text",
  you can also use HTML:  
  `inline <span style="color:red">colored</span> text`.

- For systematic styling of existing or custom elements, you need to use **_CSS_**.
  For example, including the following anywhere
  in a Markdown document will turn all level 1 headers (`#`) red:
  
  ```
  <style>
  h1 {color: red}
  </style>
  ```

<hr style="height:1pt; visibility:hidden;" />

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
#### Example Pandoc commands _(Click to expand)_
Of course, you haven't learned how to use commands in the Unix shell yet,
but once you do, these are example Pandoc commands to render Markdown files:

```sh
pandoc README.md > README.html
pandoc -o README.pdf README.md
```

The `pandoc` command is available at OSC.
:::
